newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African metal industry wage talks end in dispute.
newsitem.headline: S.African metal industry wage talks end in dispute.

text.p: Wage increase negotiations between employers and workers in South Africa's metal and engineering industry ended in dispute on Thursday, the Steel and Engineering Industries Federation of South Africa (Seifsa) said.
"The third round of this year's negotiations between employers and trade unions..., held in Johannesburg today, ended in dispute," Seifsa, the employers' body, said in a statement.
All the industry's unions rejected the final employer wage increase offer of between eight and 8.5 percent on scheduled and actual wages.
The unions' wage increase demands range from 13 to 23 percent.

The National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa, the Chemical Workers Industrial Union, the National Employees' Trade Union, the South African Workers Union and the Mine Workers' Union declared a dispute with the employer parties.

The South African Electrical Workers Association, the Steel, Engineering and Allied Workers Union of South Africa, Metal and Electrical Workers Union and the Radio, Television, Electronics and Allied Workers' Union reserved their positions but did not declare a dispute.
"The parties have agreed to consider what steps should be taken to resolve the dispute at a meeting of the National Industrial Council to be held on June 25."
